item.title: The Little Book of Generative AI Foundations: An Intuitive Mathematical Primer
item.description: This book provides a compact, derivation-oriented introduction to the mathematical foundations of modern generative artificial intelligence. Rather than surveying every recent architecture or implementation detail, it develops a coherent route through the ideas connecting major families of generative models, from PCA, probabilistic PCA, variational autoencoders, and diffusion models to normalising flows, autoregressive factorisations, GANs, Wasserstein GANs, and energy-based models. The aim is to make the structure of generative modelling more accessible without removing the mathematical substance needed to understand how these models are derived and related. The book is intended as a foundation-building primer for mathematically curious researchers, practitioners, and students.

item.title: Who broke CI this time?
item.description: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners mean that when a job hangs, the first question is always the same: is it me or is it GitHub? So I built one page that answers it. runner-watch reads each runner's process tree and socket table through yeet's system graph, once a second, to show the whole fleet at a glance: who's busy, what step is stuck and on what, and whether the listener still has its long-poll open to GitHub. No agent inside the job, the runner software untouched, and the whole deploy is one service.toml.

item.title: How reliable are confidence scores from language models?
item.description: The release of TypeSafe’s Jev brought attention to so-called decision models. These models are designed to classify predefined choices quickly. Given information, a question and possible answers, decision models return a probability for each option. We use the probability assigned to the chosen answer as its confidence score—the model’s estimate of how likely that answer is to be correct.

item.title: Stringman from Neufangled Robotics
item.description: In robotics, price is basically actuator count. Stringman reaches an entire room with four motors, hanging its gripper from lines anchored in the ceiling corners. Working from above, it reaches floors too cluttered for any wheeled or legged robot. And since the lifting force is shared by all motors, payload capacity scales with their combined torque instead of a single actuator's, peaking near the center of the room where the lines share the load most evenly.

item.title: I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere)
item.description:
This video examines the amount of location information carried by inaudible background sounds, using the Doppler effect to locate a reference recording within ~100m, and only needing (in some cases) less 1-min of audio. This video raises awareness of these capabilities and closes by discussing preventative measures one could take.
Methodology: Aircraft position, altitude, and velocity data were sourced from ADS-B data and filtered in Python using ICAO type-code classification for propeller vs jet types. For each candidate location on a 200m grid, the closest point of approach (CPA) and sound propagation delay were computed from 3D slant distance, using a digital elevation model (DEM).
Doppler curve spectrogram measurements constrained each event's velocity and CPA slant distance. Candidates were then filtered by the 920-second offset between two flyovers, plus a silence constraint. The exact Doppler curve each candidate would hear was modelled, using emission-time radial velocity from interpolated ADS-B data.
Modelled doppler curves were scored against the observed spectrogram using a locked two-event scoring method. This corrected for measurement error on CPA time & fundamental frequency, while preserving the purely physics-derived temporal offset between the two events.
The pipeline was repeated again for a single 1-min clip of known time, US-wide search, and again, successfully scored the true location 1st.
Lastly, preventative measures were assessed, including rationale behind why common signal processing fixes fail (high-pass filtering, drowning out, and phone call compression/noise reduction).
This video is an educational demonstration of acoustics, signal processing, and data analysis using publicly available data. No code or tools are being released.
Link to full recording: https://youtu.be/4CxVxuMVkMc
